title: deprecation-timestamp-schema-negotiation-shim
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We observed recurring issues when newer clients push schema v2 features (structured output markers, tool call envelopes, streaming meta events) while older downstream services and SDKs still expect the v1 payload shapes. This PR adds a lightweight negotiation shim and a Deprecation-Timestamp header to make deprecations explicit and enable graceful fallback. The shim negotiates the best supported response schema per-connection using a new Prefer-Schema-Version request header or falls back to heuristics (client User-Agent, observed request fields). It also normalizes streaming payloads so older consumers receive v1-compatible chunks while v2-capable clients get richer structured events. Changes include: 1) new header "Deprecation-Timestamp" emitted alongside deprecation log entries and surfaced to customers in the Console; 2) Prefer-Schema-Version request header support (v1, v2, auto); 3) a negotiation component in the OpenAI-compat layer that selects and records the effective schema; 4) a streaming adapter that injects "schema_version" metadata into chunk events and rewrites tool/function call envelopes for backcompat; 5) a runtime metric (api.schema_negotiation.fallback_count) and traces for end-to-end visibility. Backwards compatibility: when negotiation determines a client is v1-only we perform minimal transformations: remove structured 'blocks' field, translate function-call objects to legacy tool format, and emit simplified stream events. For v2 clients we preserve enriched structured output and new streaming control events. Migration notes: publish Deprecation-Timestamp and FAQ in docs, bump SDKs to read Prefer-Schema-Version; servers will continue accepting both shapes for the next 6 months with audit alerts enabled. Testing and rollout: unit tests for version selector, integration tests across streaming and tool-calling flows, canary run on 5% of traffic with real-time dashboards. See rollout section below for gradual ramp plan and rollback triggers.

diff_snippets: + func EmitDeprecationTimestamp(w http.ResponseWriter, ts time.Time) { w.Header().Set("Deprecation-Timestamp", ts.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)) }
+ header := req.Header.Get("Prefer-Schema-Version") // values: v1, v2, auto
+ add metric: api.schema_negotiation.fallback_count++ when negotiation falls back to v1
review_comments: Liam Chen (2025-11-13): Nice isolation of negotiation logic. Two concerns: make the heuristics for 'auto' explicit and ensure we don't accidentally oscillate schema choices mid-stream. Please add a sticky binding per-connection.
Author - Ava Martinez (2025-11-13): Added sticky binding in negotiator.go, explicitly documented heuristic order (Prefer header, explicit SDK flag, User-Agent hint, probes).
Riya Patel (2025-11-14): Can we include a short-circuit to skip rewrite when payload size or latency constraints are tight? Streaming rewrite adds small CPU costs on p95 workloads.
Author - Ava Martinez (2025-11-14): Added opt-out config via runtime flag 'schema_rewrite_budget_ms' and a microbenchmark showing <1% p95 regression for our default budget.
Diego Alvarez (2025-11-16): Integration tests look good. Please add a canary dashboard tile for negotiation fallback rate before merging.
Author - Ava Martinez (2025-11-16): Dashboard tile added (observability-pack). CI re-run after test flakiness fix passed. Approved by reviewers.
testing: Unit tests: negotiator heuristics, rewrite rules, chunk annotation. Integration: e2e flows for streaming v1->v1, v2->v2, v2->v1 fallback with tool calls. Canary: 5% traffic on a single region for 48h with metrics tracked. Load microbenchmarks added to perf-canary. All tests green in CI after one flaky test was patched.
rollout: Canary 5% (48h) -> ramp 25% (72h) -> ramp 100% over next 7 days. Rollback triggers: fallback rate > 2% above baseline, p95 latency > +15%, or error rate increase > 0.3%. Console feature flag 'enable_schema_negotiator' allows immediate rollback per-customer.
release_notes:
- Added API header 'Deprecation-Timestamp' to communicate planned removals and timelines.
- Supported new request header 'Prefer-Schema-Version' (values: v1, v2, auto).
- OpenAI-compat layer now negotiates response schema per-connection and performs safe runtime shims for older clients.
- Streaming responses now include 'schema_version' metadata in chunk events for observability.
- No immediate breaking changes; v1 and v2 shapes remain accepted during rollover period.
observability_changes: New metric: api.schema_negotiation.fallback_count, new trace spans: negotiator.select_schema and streaming.rewrite. Added dashboard tile to observability-pack and an alert when fallback rate spikes.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps transformation rules minimal and reversible. Longer-term follow-ups: 1) telemetry-driven automatic deprecation notices to SDK users, 2) formal version negotiation protocol and wire-level handshake for persistent connections.
hotfix_related_incidents: None. This was preemptive work after an internal postmortem on schema-related panics in a partner integration. The incident notes are referenced in ENG-1507.
ci_artifacts: CI produced integration test logs, microbenchmark numbers, and a perf-canary report attached to the PR. All artifacts linked in the CI run.
security_review: No sensitive surface changes. Negotiator runs entirely in the API layer and does not expose new customer data. Security reviewed by SRE and sec-team; no findings.
support_instructions: If customers report missing fields after deploy, ask for request headers and User-Agent string. If they need immediate v2 features, set Accept header or Prefer-Schema-Version to v2 and open ticket SUP-982.
